formation.title: The Maratha Swarajya
formation.text:
The Deccan trembles. What began as the defiance of a single Bhonsle chieftain has become something the Mughal padishahs and Bijapur sultans never imagined: a sovereign Maratha state, forged in the hill forts of the Western Ghats and baptized in the blood of a hundred ambushes. The coronation at Raigad has given this new nation a crown, but the harder question remains: what kind of nation shall this be? Will we remain the swift raiders of the hills, the masters of ganimi kava who can bleed any empire dry? Or will we build the institutions of governance that transform a warrior kingdom into a lasting civilization?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the shadow in the mountains.

modifiers.name: Ganimi Kava
modifiers.text: The art of guerrilla warfare perfected by Shivaji Maharaj: swift strikes from hill forts, ambushes in mountain passes, and the relentless harrying of vastly superior forces. Speed, terrain, and audacity replace numbers and heavy armor.

options.text: We shall build a kingdom for all Marathas.

modifiers.name: Hindavi Swarajya
modifiers.text: The dream of Hindu self-rule that Shivaji proclaimed at his coronation in Raigad: an independent state governed by its own people, administered through the Ashtapradhan council, and sustained by the devotion of the Marathi-speaking heartland.

advances.name: Yadava Heritage
advances.text: The Marathas trace their lineage to the Yadava dynasty that ruled the Deccan from Devagiri. This ancient heritage provides legitimacy and a tradition of cavalry warfare across the plateau.

advances.name: Warkari Devotion
advances.text: The Warkari tradition of pilgrimage to Pandharpur, sustained by the abhangs of saints like Dnyaneshwar and Namdev, forges a common spiritual identity among the Marathi people.

event.title: The Saints of the Warkari Path
event.text: From the banks of the Indrayani to the temple of Vithoba at Pandharpur, a river of pilgrims flows each year: barefoot farmers, potters, and weavers who sing the abhangs of Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram as they walk. The Warkari movement has done what no army could: it has given the Marathi people a shared spiritual identity that transcends caste and village. Tukaram's verses declare that devotion knows no birth, and Dnyaneshwar's Dnyaneshwari made the wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita accessible in the language of the common people. This movement can be embraced as the spiritual foundation of our state, or channeled as a force for social reform and literacy.

options.text: Pandharpur shall be our spiritual heart.

modifiers.name: Light of Pandharpur
modifiers.text: The devotional fervor of the Warkari pilgrimage unites the Marathi people in shared faith and cultural pride.

options.text: The saints teach us that all castes are equal before God.

modifiers.name: Caste-Blind Devotion
modifiers.text: The radical egalitarianism of the Bhakti saints breaks down social barriers and spreads literacy through vernacular devotional poetry.

advances.name: Deccan Agriculture
advances.text: The black cotton soils of the Deccan plateau and the seasonal monsoon rains support a distinctive agricultural system centered on millet, pulses, and cotton.

advances.name: Marathi Literary Tradition
advances.text: The Dnyaneshwari and other works in the Marathi language create a literate culture that transcends the Sanskrit-educated elite, bringing philosophy and governance to the common people.

advances.name: Western Ghats Mastery
advances.text: The rugged terrain of the Western Ghats (steep ravines, dense forests, and narrow passes) is the natural fortress of the Marathi people, and they have learned to move through it as no outsider can.

advances.name: Gadkot Tradition
advances.text: The tradition of building fortifications atop the hills and ridges of the Western Ghats creates a network of impregnable strongpoints, the gads, that anchor Maratha military power.

advances.name: Mavla Hillmen
advances.text: The mavlas are hardy infantry from the Maval region of the Western Ghats, expert in hill fighting, ambushes, and night raids. They form the core of Shivaji's guerrilla army.

advances.name: Ganimi Kava Tactics
advances.text: Shivaji's perfection of guerrilla warfare, ganimi kava, transforms the Western Ghats into a deathtrap for conventional armies through ambushes, night raids, and feigned retreats. The Hetkari marksmen of the Konkan open the trap with their firelocks, and the Mavla swordsmen close it.

event.title: The Art of Ganimi Kava
event.text: While the great armies of the Mughal Empire march in ponderous columns across the Deccan plains, our fighters vanish into the folds of the Western Ghats like monsoon mist. Shivaji Maharaj has perfected the art of ganimi kava: guerrilla warfare that turns every ravine into an ambush site, every hill fort into an impregnable refuge, and every moonless night into a battlefield. At Pratapgad, a Maratha force annihilated the army of Afzal Khan. At Sinhagad, Tanaji Malusare's men scaled sheer cliffs in darkness to seize a fortress the Mughals thought unassailable. These are not isolated victories; they are a military doctrine that will define Maratha warfare for generations.

options.text: The mountains are our fortress, and the night is our ally.

advances.name: Ashtapradhan Council
advances.text: The council of eight ministers (Peshwa, Amatya, Sachiv, Mantri, Senapati, Sumant, Nyayadhish, and Panditrao) provides the administrative framework for the Maratha state.

advances.name: Coronation Traditions
advances.text: The coronation ceremony at Raigad, conducted according to Vedic rites, establishes the Chhatrapati as a sovereign Hindu king: a direct challenge to Mughal supremacy over the Deccan.

advances.name: Deccan Trade Routes
advances.text:
The great trade routes connecting the Konkan coast to the Deccan interior carry cotton, spices, and textiles, making the Maratha heartland a hub of commercial activity.

Available in: Koshti Karkhana

advances.name: Fort Network
advances.text: The systematic construction and maintenance of hill forts across the Western Ghats creates an interlocking defensive network where each fort supports its neighbors.

advances.name: Konkan Naval Power
advances.text: Under admirals like Kanhoji Angre, the Maratha navy dominates the Konkan coast from Surat to south of Mumbai, using fast gallivats and grabs to challenge even the European maritime powers.

advances.name: Shiledar System
advances.text: The shiledar cavalry system, where horsemen provide their own mounts and weapons in exchange for a monthly salary, creates a self-reliant force of light cavalry raiders.

advances.name: Chauth System
advances.text: The chauth, a levy of one-quarter of total revenue collected from neighboring territories, becomes the financial backbone of the Maratha state and a powerful instrument of political control.

advances.name: Abhang Poetry
advances.text: The devotional verses of Tukaram and other Bhakti poet-saints, composed in everyday Marathi, create a body of literature that gives the common people access to spiritual and philosophical ideas.

advances.name: Coastal Raiding
advances.text: Maratha naval tactics emphasize fast, maneuverable vessels that close from astern to avoid cannon broadsides, then board enemy ships in fierce hand-to-hand combat.

advances.name: Peshwa Rise
advances.text: The office of the Peshwa, originally the chief minister of the Ashtapradhan, gradually becomes the real seat of power in the Maratha state, producing brilliant administrators and generals.

advances.name: Bargir Cavalry
advances.text: Unlike the self-equipped shiledar, bargir cavalrymen are provided horses and weapons by the state, creating a more disciplined and centrally controlled cavalry force.

advances.name: Peshwa Bureaucracy
advances.text: The Peshwa administration in Pune develops a sophisticated bureaucratic system with detailed record-keeping, standardized revenue collection, and professional administrators.

advances.name: Confederacy Structure
advances.text: The Maratha Confederacy evolves into a federal system where powerful houses (Holkar, Scindia, Gaekwad, and Bhonsale) govern vast territories while acknowledging the nominal supremacy of the Chhatrapati.

event.title: The Maratha Confederacy
event.text: Under the Peshwas, the Maratha state has evolved into something unprecedented: a confederacy of powerful houses, each commanding their own armies and territories, yet bound together by shared loyalty to the Chhatrapati and the dream of Hindavi Swarajya. The Holkars hold Indore, the Scindias command Gwalior, the Gaekwads govern Baroda, and the Bhonsales rule Nagpur. Together they have pushed Maratha power from the Deccan to the gates of Delhi itself. Baji Rao's cavalry raids have humiliated the Mughal emperor in his own capital. But this very success raises a question: should we bind these great houses more tightly under Peshwa authority, or give them the freedom to expand as they will?

options.text: Unity under the Peshwa shall be our strength.

modifiers.name: Peshwa Ascendancy
modifiers.text: The great Maratha houses are bound together under the administrative authority of the Peshwa, creating a unified confederacy.

options.text: Let each sardar carry our banner to new horizons.

modifiers.name: Maratha Horsemen Unbound
modifiers.text: The sardars of the confederacy ride forth independently, carrying Maratha power to every corner of the subcontinent.

advances.name: Grab Warships
advances.text: The grab, a larger and more heavily armed vessel than the gallivat, serves as the backbone of the Maratha fleet: capable of engaging European ships on more equal terms.

advances.name: Sardeshmukhi Rights
advances.text: The sardeshmukhi, an additional ten percent levy beyond the chauth, asserts the Maratha sovereign's claim as hereditary head of all deshmukhs across the Deccan.

advances.name: Deccan Cotton Trade
advances.text:
The Deccan's black cotton soils produce some of India's finest raw cotton, feeding a thriving textile industry that exports cloth across the Indian Ocean trading world. The Peshwas settle weavers from Paithan at Yeola, where silk and gold thread go into the saris of the court.

Available in: Koshti Karkhana

advances.name: European Military Methods
advances.text:
The pragmatic adoption of European military techniques (field artillery, infantry drill, and modern fortification) transforms the Maratha army without abandoning its cavalry traditions.

Available in: Tophkhana

event.title: European Methods and Maratha Arms
event.text: The arrival of European powers on the Indian coast has brought more than trade goods and missionaries: it has brought new methods of warfare. European-drilled infantry, field artillery, and fortification techniques have proven devastatingly effective against traditional armies. The Marathas, ever pragmatic, have begun to adapt. French adventurers like Benoit de Boigne have trained Maratha infantry in European drill, while Maratha smiths have learned to cast European-style cannon in the tophkhanas of Pune and Satara. The question is whether we embrace these foreign methods wholesale or selectively adopt what serves us while maintaining our distinctive cavalry traditions.

options.text: Modernize the army with European weapons and drill.

modifiers.name: Tophkhana Modernization
modifiers.text: European artillery and infantry drill have been adopted wholesale, transforming the Maratha army into a modern fighting force.

options.text: Study the Europeans. And use their own methods against them.

modifiers.name: Playing the Great Game
modifiers.text: Maratha diplomats study European methods of statecraft, intelligence, and alliance-building to turn the colonizers' own tools against them.

advances.name: Gardis Bodyguard
advances.text: The Gardis are an elite bodyguard corps trained in European methods, serving as the personal guard of the Peshwa and as shock troops in pitched battles.

advances.name: Territorial Administration
advances.text: As Maratha territory expands across the subcontinent, the Peshwa government develops systems for administering distant provinces, appointing deputies, and maintaining control over far-flung garrisons.

advances.name: Maratha Resilience
advances.text: Even after the catastrophe of Panipat in 1761, the Marathas regroup and recover within a decade, retaking Delhi and reasserting control over much of India: a testament to the depth of Maratha military and administrative capacity.

advances.name: Konkan Trade Network
advances.text: The Maratha-controlled ports of the Konkan coast develop into a thriving commercial network, linking the agricultural interior to the maritime trade routes of the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Maval Militia Reform
advances.text: Drawing on the tradition of the mavla hillmen, reforms standardize local militia recruitment, ensuring a steady supply of trained soldiers from the Western Ghats heartland.

advances.name: Modern Artillery
advances.text: Maratha foundries in Pune and Satara produce modern field guns, while trained artillerists learn to deploy them in the European manner: a far cry from the crude bombards of earlier centuries.

advances.name: Last Peshwa Reforms
advances.text: In the twilight of the Maratha Confederacy, final administrative reforms seek to centralize authority and streamline governance, attempting to match the institutional efficiency of the British.

advances.name: Maratha Identity
advances.text: The legacy of Shivaji, the poetry of the Bhakti saints, and centuries of self-governance forge a distinctive Marathi cultural identity that endures beyond the political life of the empire.

advances.name: Fortress Modernization
advances.text: The ancient gad hill forts are upgraded with modern bastions, gun emplacements, and European-style defensive works to resist artillery bombardment.

advances.name: Industrial Deccan
advances.text:
The Deccan's mineral wealth, cotton production, and skilled artisan traditions provide the foundation for early industrial development.

Available in: Tophkhana

advances.name: Deccan Independence
advances.text: The culmination of centuries of Maratha governance: a self-sufficient Deccan state with its own institutions, economy, and cultural identity, independent of outside domination.

destiny.name: Maratha Destiny
destiny.text: With the Deccan united under the Maratha banner, the path forward diverges. The Swarajya stands at a crossroads between the sword and the plough, between conquest and civilization.

event.title: The Destiny of the Marathas
event.text: The Maratha state has proven its permanence. What began as the rebellion of a single chieftain against the sultans of the Deccan has become an established kingdom with institutions, traditions, and ambitions that reach far beyond the Western Ghats. The question that consumed Shivaji's court (whether the Marathas are raiders or rulers) now demands an answer written not in the language of debate, but in the language of deeds.

options.text: Our destiny awaits.

destiny.name: Lord of the Deccan
destiny.text: Secure the western approaches by seizing Surat and push into Malwa by taking Gwalior. With these strongpoints in hand, no army can threaten the Maratha heartland.

conditions.text: Own Surat, or a subject owns it
Own Gwalior, or a subject owns it

event.title: Lord of the Deccan
event.text: Surat's warehouses and Gwalior's fortress are ours. The old sultanates that once divided this land are broken, and the Maratha standard flies over the western trade routes and the gateway to Hindustan. Every merchant who passes through Surat pays tribute to the Swarajya. Every army that contemplates invasion must reckon with the fortress of Gwalior at its flank. The Deccan is no longer a contested frontier. It is a Maratha domain.

options.text: The Deccan bows to the Maratha lion.

destiny.name: The Northern March
destiny.text: Baji Rao rode to the gates of Delhi and back in a single campaign. Now make it permanent: plant the Maratha flag in Delhi and secure the Malwa plateau through Ujjain.

conditions.text: Own Delhi, or a subject owns it
Own Ujjain, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Road to Delhi
event.text: Delhi has fallen. The city that for centuries was the seat of Muslim sovereignty over Hindustan now acknowledges Maratha supremacy. Ujjain, the ancient capital of Malwa, secures our western flank. But an empire won by the sword must be held by more than the sword. Do we ride as Baji Rao did: fast, relentless, overwhelming our enemies before they can react? Or do we methodically reduce every fortress and strongpoint, building an unbreakable chain of control from the Deccan to the Yamuna?

options.text: Ride like Baji Rao: strike before they know we are coming.

modifiers.name: Baji Rao's Charge
modifiers.text: The lightning campaign doctrine of Baji Rao I: strike fast, strike hard, and be gone before the enemy can marshal a response. Speed is the weapon of the outnumbered.

options.text: Every fort taken is a fort that cannot threaten us.

modifiers.name: Strategic Patience
modifiers.text: The methodical reduction of enemy strongpoints through prolonged siege, turning every conquest into an unshakable possession. Patience wins what speed cannot hold.

destiny.name: Hindu Pad Padshahi
destiny.text: The dream of a Hindu empire stretching from the Deccan to the Punjab. Take Agra and Lahore, command the greatest army on the subcontinent, and claim the title the Mughals once held.

conditions.text: Own Agra, or a subject owns it
Own Lahore, or a subject owns it

event.title: Hindu Pad Padshahi
event.text: From the Indus to the Narmada, from the Thar to the Bay of Bengal, the Maratha empire commands a domain that surpasses even the greatest Mughal ambitions. Agra's marble palaces and Lahore's golden temples are now Maratha possessions. The Hindu Pad Padshahi (the supremacy of Hindu kings) is no longer a dream whispered in the courts of Raigad. It is the reality of the subcontinent. But supreme power brings supreme choices. Shall we rule through the strength of a vast military machine, drawing mercenaries and adventurers from across the world? Or shall we build the commercial and naval infrastructure to sustain our empire through trade as much as through arms?

options.text: Our armies shall be the pillar of empire.

modifiers.name: Hindu Padshahi
modifiers.text: A vast military machine fueled by mercenary armies and professional soldiers, projecting Maratha power across the subcontinent through sheer force of arms.

options.text: Empire endures through commerce, not conquest alone.

modifiers.name: Maratha Imperator
modifiers.text: An empire sustained by trade and naval power as much as by armies, with merchants and admirals serving alongside generals in the expansion of Maratha dominion.

destiny.name: Foundation of Swaraj
destiny.text: Before the Marathas can build a lasting civilization, the kingdom needs a seat and a treasury. Raigad, the hill capital where Shivaji was crowned, must be built up, and the treasury filled.

conditions.text: We hold Raigarh and it has at least 18 development

event.title: The Foundation of Self-Rule
event.text: The dream of Hindavi Swarajya was never merely about independence from foreign rule. It was about building a state worthy of its people: one where the revenue systems are fair, the administration is competent, and the wealth of the land serves all who work it. A full treasury has given the Maratha state a financial strength that rivals that of any European power. The palaces, the market street and the reservoirs of Raigad speak louder than any proclamation: this is a civilization that can sustain itself.

options.text: Swarajya is built on the prosperity of its people.

destiny.name: Deccani Prosperity
destiny.text: Extend the chauth system into Gujarat by taking Baroda, fill the treasury, and ensure Deccan cotton flows through the capital's markets. Wealth is the sinew of self-rule.

conditions.text: Own Baroda, or a subject owns it

children.text: Cotton is produced in the market
Cotton is traded in the market

event.title: Deccani Prosperity
event.text: The chauth offices of Baroda collect revenue from the richest trade routes of Gujarat. Cotton from the Deccan's black soil flows through our markets to the world. The treasury overflows. Pune has become not merely a military capital but a center of intellectual life: poets, astronomers, and administrators gather in its courts. But prosperity creates its own dilemmas. Do we invest in the life of the mind, supporting scholars and attracting foreign expertise to build our knowledge? Or do we pour our wealth into the cotton trade itself, building the ships and ports that will make the Deccan the textile workshop of the Indian Ocean?

options.text: Pune shall become the Athens of the Deccan.

modifiers.name: Pune Intellectuals
modifiers.text: The scholars, astronomers, and administrators of Pune transform the Maratha capital into a center of learning that attracts talent from across the Indian Ocean world.

options.text: Deccan cotton shall clothe the world.

modifiers.name: Cotton Empire
modifiers.text: Deccan cotton, woven into the finest textiles and shipped on Maratha vessels, becomes the foundation of an economic empire that rivals any military conquest.

destiny.name: The Deccani Golden Age
destiny.text: Build a civilization that rivals any on earth: a Deccan of literate citizens, thriving markets, and a cultural tradition that endures for centuries. Raise Pune from a market town into a great city, found libraries in three of our towns, and fill the coffers.

conditions.text: We hold Pune and it has at least 41 development
A Library stands in at least 3 of our towns

event.title: The Deccani Golden Age
event.text: What Shivaji planted has grown into a civilization. The Deccan is no longer defined by the empires that conquered it. It is defined by what its own people have built. A literate population reads Marathi poetry and debates governance in coffee houses. The libraries of our towns spread ideas from village to village. The treasury is the envy of kings. Foreign ambassadors come not to dictate terms but to seek alliance. This is the Deccani Golden Age. But how shall it be remembered? As an age of diplomatic mastery and harmonious governance? Or as an age of spiritual and cultural flowering that transcends political boundaries?

options.text: We shall be the architects of a new order.

modifiers.name: Deccani Renaissance
modifiers.text: A flowering of statecraft and governance that integrates diverse peoples under a system of shared prosperity and institutional excellence.

options.text: Let the light of the Deccan illuminate all faiths.

modifiers.name: Marathi Enlightenment
modifiers.text: The spiritual and cultural traditions of the Bhakti movement mature into a broader philosophy of religious tolerance and devotional renewal that transcends sectarian boundaries.

units.name: Mavla Hillmen
units.text: Hardy infantry from the Maval region of the Western Ghats, experts in hill fighting, night raids, and guerrilla warfare. They are the backbone of Shivaji's ganimi kava doctrine.

units.name: Hetkari Marksmen
units.text: Musketeers from the Konkan lowlands below the Ghats, the second arm of Shivaji's infantry. They climb like the Mavlas and shoot better than anyone in the Deccan, but they are not the men to send in sword in hand.

units.name: Shiledar Cavalry
units.text: Self-equipped light cavalry who provide their own horses and weapons. Fast, independent, and skilled at raiding deep behind enemy lines.

units.name: Bargir Cavalry
units.text: State-equipped cavalry who receive their mounts and arms from the government. More disciplined than the shiledar, they serve as the heavy striking arm of the Maratha army.

units.name: Gardis
units.text: Elite bodyguard infantry trained in European military methods. Professional soldiers who serve as the Peshwa's personal guard and shock troops in pitched battles.

units.name: Gallivat
units.text: A small, fast coastal warboat with oars and a single mast, crewed by fifty to sixty men. Used for boarding actions, coastal raids, and harrying larger European vessels.

units.name: Grab
units.text: A larger Maratha warship of up to four hundred tons, armed with cannon and carrying over a hundred crew. Capable of engaging European ships in close combat.

units.name: Silahdar
units.text: Reformed militia infantry drawn from the Maval highlands, drilled in improved formations and equipped with standardized weapons by the state.

units.name: Maratha Field Gun
units.text: Modern field artillery cast in Maratha foundries, crewed by trained artillerists and capable of sustained bombardment in the European fashion.

buildings.name: Gad
buildings.text: A hilltop fortification built on the steep ridges of the Western Ghats. Its commanding position, sheer approaches, and thick stone walls make it virtually impregnable to assault.

buildings.name: Chauth Kacheri
buildings.text: A revenue office that administers the collection of chauth, one quarter of the territory's revenue, on behalf of the Maratha sovereign.

buildings.name: Warkari Math
buildings.text: A monastery associated with the Warkari tradition of devotional pilgrimage. Centers of Bhakti learning, abhang poetry, and communal worship of Vithoba.

buildings.name: Tophkhana
buildings.text: An artillery foundry producing European-style cannon and firearms. Staffed by skilled metalworkers and often supervised by foreign advisors.

buildings.name: Angre Shipyard
buildings.text: A naval dockyard on the Konkan coast, built in the tradition of Admiral Kanhoji Angre, producing the gallivats and grabs that dominate the western Indian seaboard.

buildings.name: Peshwa Daftar
buildings.text: The administrative chancery of the Peshwa government, maintaining detailed records of revenue, military deployments, and diplomatic correspondence.

buildings.name: Bastion Fort
buildings.text: A modernized fortification combining the traditional hilltop position of the Maratha gad with European-style star bastions and angled gun emplacements.

buildings.name: Maratha Darbar
buildings.text: The imperial court of the Maratha empire, where the Chhatrapati receives tribute from vassal kings and foreign ambassadors. A symbol of Hindu Pad Padshahi made manifest.

buildings.name: Sharada Peeth
buildings.text: A great academy of learning in the tradition of the ancient Sharada Peetha, where scholars study philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, and the arts of governance.

buildings.name: Koshti Karkhana
buildings.text: A weaver's workshop where the koshti caste produces fine Deccan cotton textiles. The Maratha heartland's cotton was prized across the Indian Ocean trade network.

list.name: Ashta Pradhan
list.text: The Council of Eight Ministers established by Shivaji Maharaj at his coronation at Raigad on 6 June 1674. The Peshwa, Amatya, Mantri, Sachiv, Sumant, Senapati, Nyayadhish, and Panditrao were each assigned defined portfolios: prime minister, finance, intelligence, secretariat, foreign affairs, military, justice, and religion. Two of the eight (Nyayadhish and Panditrao) were reserved for Brahmin learned-castes, anchoring religious sanction in the institution and transforming the Maratha state from a personal warband into a written constitutional structure.

list.name: Peshwa Daftar
list.text: The Pune chancery of the hereditary Peshwa minister. Originating in Shivaji's Ashta Pradhan as a single portfolio, the office became hereditary in the Bhat family of Chitpavan Brahmins after Balaji Vishwanath (1713-1720) and consolidated as the de facto seat of Maratha sovereignty under Bajirao I (1720-1740) and Balaji Bajirao Nanasaheb (1740-1761). Pune replaced Satara as the operative capital. The daftar issued sanads, recorded revenue assignments, and routed correspondence with the great sardar houses, becoming the institutional spine of the Confederacy.

list.name: Saranjami System
list.text: The Maratha analog of mansabdari, in which the state assigned tracts of revenue (saranjam) to sardars and military officers in lieu of cash pay. The grants were originally non-hereditary and contingent on continued military service, but under the later Peshwas they hardened into hereditary holdings of the great houses: Holkar in Indore, Scindia in Gwalior, Gaekwad in Baroda. The system fed the Confederacy's vast cavalry armies cheaply but progressively starved the central treasury and bound revenue to sardar loyalty rather than crown command.

list.name: Watandari Registry
list.text: The Maratha state inherited from its Yadava and Bahmani predecessors a dense layer of hereditary village officeholders. The patil was the village headman, the kulkarni the village accountant, and below them the bara balutedar of twelve traditional service-castes. Shivaji deliberately confirmed these watans to bind the rural Marathi-speaking gentry to the new state. The grants were inalienable and inheritable, locking local revenue administration into the hands of the existing Deshmukh and Deshpande lineages: a form of structural autonomy crown reformers found almost impossible to dislodge.

list.name: Chauth and Sardeshmukhi
list.text: The twin tribute claims that defined Maratha expansion. The chauth was a 25% levy on revenue collected from territories the Marathas claimed protection over, while the sardeshmukhi added a further 10% as the chief headman's right. Both rights were extracted by treaty from the dying Mughal empire after Bahadur Shah's death and formalized by Chhatrapati Shahu after 1719. They funded the Confederacy's expansion deep into north India but cast every tributary state as a temporary revenue source rather than an integrated province, and earned the Marathas a reputation across Hindustan for predatory extraction.

list.name: Huzur Daftar
list.text: The central record office at Pune, the institutional memory of the Confederacy. Established under the early Peshwas and perfected under Nana Phadnavis (1761-1800), the daftar audited every saranjam grant, traced revenue from village to treasury, and kept the correspondence registers that bound the sardar houses to the Peshwa's seal. Nana's twelve-year regency for Madhavrao II rested entirely on his command of the daftar's records; his death in 1800 exposed how completely the Confederacy had come to depend on its archive.

list.name: Pentarchy of the Confederacy
list.text: The institutionalized practice by which Peshwa directives required the cooperation of the five great sardar houses: Holkar at Indore, Scindia at Gwalior, Bhonsle at Nagpur, Gaekwad at Baroda, and the Peshwa himself at Pune. By the 1760s these houses fielded their own armies, conducted their own diplomacy, and treated Pune as primus inter pares rather than sovereign. The arrangement let the Confederacy project power across an enormous territory but turned every campaign into a coalition negotiation: the disagreement among the five at Panipat in 1761 contributed to the catastrophe there.
